purpose: Calibrate the fixed AutoCon relation-loss weight under one frozen current-tree MambaACFAutoCon configuration before any fresh test-producing replication.
research_question: With the same static raw train-only ACF prior, causal embedding, Mamba architecture, relation sampler, optimizer, and seed, does lambda 0.01 or 0.03 improve validation forecasting loss relative to the identical lambda=0 relation null?
evidence_boundary: This is an unauthorized, validation-only H96 calibration screen on ETTh1 and traffic with three fresh seeds. It does not evaluate the test split, is not confirmatory evidence, and cannot support a publication claim.
claim_boundary: The relation objective regularizes the representation branch by default; it does not directly supervise forecast ACF memory or its gate because mamba_acf_repr_fusion is fixed false. The screen may select one fixed lambda for a later independent evaluation only; it cannot establish a general Mamba, ACF, signed-relation, accuracy, or speed claim.

required_before_launch: human review of the validation-only, two-dataset, H96, three-seed scope
confirm the current source/environment hashes and the raw train-only sidecar contract
confirm a fresh empty output root and freeze this JSON with an approved launch sidecar
confirm that no test split will be evaluated or used to choose lambda
confirm that CE/sign diagnostics and relation coverage will be retained in loss_logs.json

seed_policy.reason: Fresh seeds relative to completed 2021-2023 exploratory screens and separate from currently registered mechanism candidates.
seed_policy.artifact_policy: Use a fresh output root. Retain source snapshot, environment, dataset hashes, plan/config hashes, manifest, train-only ACF sidecar, checkpoint, and loss_logs.json. Do not copy historical metrics, checkpoints, or selected lambda values into this matrix.

phases.name: relation_lambda_calibration_h96
phases.purpose: One architecture and one training contract; only the explicitly registered relation-loss weight varies. Lambda zero retains the AutoCon model, relation objective, sampler, and diagnostics, but contributes zero auxiliary gradient.

lambda_calibration_contract.selection_data: validation loss from the retained best checkpoint and loss_logs.json only
lambda_calibration_contract.common_configuration: All non-lambda architecture, optimizer, sampler, ACF prior, source, and seed fields are fixed by the single phase.
lambda_calibration_contract.selection_rule: Before any test-producing evaluation, freeze one global lambda using only validation data. Report all seed-level validation values and paired ratios versus lambda zero. A non-zero lambda may advance only if neither dataset has mean validation MSE worse than lambda zero by more than 0.5 percent; otherwise retain lambda zero. If both non-zero lambdas satisfy the rule, prefer the smaller lambda unless the larger one improves the unweighted mean validation log-MSE ratio by at least 0.2 percent.
lambda_calibration_contract.post_selection_rule: Any chosen lambda requires a new independently seeded, separately approved test-producing replication. No test replay or architecture change is part of this calibration plan.

required_diagnostics: magnitude and sign relation components when available
stopping_rules: Do not expand lambda values, datasets, horizons, sign weight, representation fusion, or architecture based on this screen.
Invalidate a coordinate if its sidecar, effective lag, source snapshot, config hash, checkpoint, loss log, or validation trajectory is missing or inconsistent.
Do not promote a non-zero lambda when either dataset is worse than the null on all three seeds or when the pre-registered validation rule rejects it.
A calibration result does not license a test claim; use a new independently seeded and approved evaluation matrix.
comparison_contract.publication_claim_boundary: This screen calibrates a fixed auxiliary-loss weight under one current-tree configuration. It cannot establish that AutoCon relation learning, signed ACF, ACF memory, Mamba, or the combined model improves forecasting generally.
